name: Beginner
description: Every adventurer starts as a Beginner on Maple Island. Learn the basics of combat with simple skills before choosing your path at level 10.
starting_level_note: Classic World starts every character at level 1 in its own economy.
starting_stats_note: Every character starts with 4 STR, 4 DEX, 4 INT and 4 LUK, and those 16 points count toward total AP.
creation_ap_note: You place your first 9 AP on the character creation screen, so pick your class before you make your character.
Every character starts with 4 in each stat. You place 9 more AP at character creation, then get 5 AP per level for STR, DEX, INT, and LUK.

ap.ap_per_level_note: You get 5 AP with each level, and you can use them on the stats you want in Character Info to make your character stronger.
ap.unused_ap_retained: Not explicitly stated. AP is placed by hand and stays where it is put: "You place every AP and SP by hand. A misplaced stat stays there until you use a cash-shop AP Reset."
ap.ap_not_reset_on_job_advancement: 1st job has no stat requirements (a 4-INT Beginner can advance to Warrior), but your AP does not reset on advancement.

sp.note: You earn 9 SP by the time you hit level 10 (1 per level-up, 9 level-ups from 1 to 10). That's exactly enough to max all three Beginner skills (3 SP each, 9 total).
sp.after_level_10_as_beginner: Not documented. MeowDB's calculators return Beginner SP = 9 at every level (model, not confirmed).
sp.calculator_caveat: The /formulas/leveling "AP and SP" calculator prints "Beginner SP = 9" for every level, including level 1. It is the level-10 total, not a starting grant. The Beginner's guide gives only "9 SP by the time you hit level 10 (1 per level-up)" (note); 1 SP at each level-up from 2 to 10, and so 0 SP at level 1, is arithmetic from that sentence, not a value any page states.

hp_mp.random_range_note: Flat gains; MeowDB: "Sampled level-ups showed zero variance." (hp_mp_gain.json)

max_level.note: MeowDB gives the game cap (Lv 100, see exp_table.json) but no Beginner-specific cap. A Beginner can stay a Beginner past level 10 (the HP/MP guide documents a level 11 Beginner advancing late); MeowDB's HP/MP calculator accepts Beginner levels 1-100.
max_level.evidence: A level 11 Beginner advanced to Warrior

stat_caps_note: Not documented on MeowDB (only Speed cap 140 and Jump cap 120, see movement.json).

statements: To advance for not only Warriors, Bowmen, and Thieves, but also Magicians, you need to be at least level 10.
1st job has no stat requirements (a 4-INT Beginner can advance to Warrior), but your AP does not reset on advancement.
job_advancement.leaving_maple_island: Shanks at the dock sails you to Lith Harbor for 300 mesos once you reach level 7.

equipment_restrictions.rule: A Beginner can equip only items with no job requirement ("Any" class) that meet the level and stat requirements.
statements: Every NPC-sold item with no class lock.
If you can't wear something, check that your character meets the level and statistic requirements.
equipment_restrictions.note: The rule is MeowDB tool logic (character builder: Beginner matches no job requirement) plus the Beginner shop category "no class lock"; it is not stated as a sentence on a mechanics page.

starter_weapons.statement: Every any-class weapon, from the 50-meso starter trio (Sword, Hand Axe, Wooden Club) up to Lv 27.
starter_weapons.creation_choice_note: Choose the Wooden Club at character creation. It has 19 W.ATK; the Sword and Hand Axe have 17.
starter_weapons.level_req_note: level_req 0 = no level requirement: the item page has no "REQ LEV" row, the Beginner shop list shows "-" in its Lv column, and MeowDB's item API gives "levelReq": 0 (checked for 541/576/585; Razor 558 has 5 on all three).
guide_advice: Club attacks one tier slower than Sword or Hand Axe, but across levels 1 to 4, the Club reaches the useful damage breakpoints more often.
At level 5, switch to Razor. Its 23 W.ATK and faster speed give every class path higher minimum and average damage than Wooden Club.

skills.name: Three Snails
skills.description: Hurls snail shells to attack monsters from long distance.
skills.damage_note: Three Snails deals the fixed damage stored for the selected skill level. Character stats, weapon stats, and target defense do not scale this fixed value.
skills.factors_statement: Affected by Skill level Conditional factors Required shell item Target hit eligibility
skills.hit_check_note: The page lists "Target hit eligibility" as a conditional factor but does not say explicitly whether the shared accuracy roll, the level-gap scale or critical hits apply to this fixed damage (gap).
skills.terrain_note: Wall and platform interactions are not confirmed for this skill.

skills.name: Recovery
skills.description: Enables the user to recover HP constantly for 30 sec.
skills.output_note: Recovery restores a fixed total amount of HP across its 30-second duration.
skills.factors_statement: Affected by Skill level Conditional factors 30-second effect duration

levels.effect: MP -5; Recover HP 24 in 30 sec. Cooldown: 2 min.
MP -10; Recover HP 48 in 30 sec. Cooldown: 2 min.
MP -15; Recover HP 72 in 30 sec. Cooldown: 2 min.

skills.name: Nimble Feet
skills.description: Enables the character to move around quickly for a short amount of time.

levels.effect: MP -4; speed +10 for 10 sec. Cooldown: 3 min.
MP -7; speed +10 for 20 sec. Cooldown: 3 min.
MP -10; speed +10 for 30 sec. Cooldown: 3 min.

skills_max_level_summary: 40 fixed damage, ranged. Consumes 1 Red Snail Shell + 5 MP per cast.
skill_order_advice: Order matters for levels 1 to 9; by 10 they're all maxed anyway. Take Nimble Feet first, then Three Snails for ranged, Recovery last.

basic_attack.mp_cost_note: Switch to basic attacks when MP is low; they cost no MP.
basic_attack.with_weapon: damage.json physical formula with the weapon's family, action multipliers and hit boxes (attack_styles.json beginner_weapons). No mastery (MasteryLevel 0 -> M = 0.08). Critical base c = 0.05, d = 0.20.
basic_attack.stat_advice: STR gives a Beginner stronger basic attacks than INT does.

bare_hands.note: MeowDB has NOTHING on unarmed damage: no Weapon Attack value, no multiplier ("Barehanded" row shows "-" for the average multiplier), no speed, and the Damage Simulator has no Beginner/unarmed option. Searched: /formulas/damage, /guides/explaining-the-damage-formula, /guides/weapon-reach, /dmg-simulator (page and JS), /character-builder JS, /classes, /classes/beginner.

death_exp_penalty.status: MeowDB's Model (MeowDB's own model of the mechanic; not a confirmed game constant)
formulas: Loss = floor(EXP to next level × (5 + 20 / LUK) / 100)
EXP after death = max(0, EXP - Loss)
notes: LUK is base LUK: the points you put in, before gear.
EXP stops at 0, so a death never takes away a level.
A Safety Charm stops the loss.
death_exp_penalty.luk_basis: The character's own base LUK: the starting 4 plus every AP placed in LUK, before equipment and buffs ("the points you put in, before gear"). Every character starts with 4 LUK, and MeowDB's calculator clamps the input to 4..999. Do not use only the allocated AP (that can be 0 and would divide by zero).
death_exp_penalty.exceptions_note: MeowDB documents NO exception for dying in town and NO Beginner exception. The only documented way to avoid the loss is a Safety Charm. Do not add exceptions from other sources without recording them as external.

beginner_perks.taxi_discount: Taxis are 90% off while you are still a Beginner.

class_page_strengths: Three Snails gives an early ranged attack (each throw uses a snail shell)
Nimble Feet gives a bit of mobility
No commitment: every job is still open
class_page_weaknesses: Skills are minor next to job skills
gaps: Bare-hand (no weapon) Weapon Attack, multiplier and attack speed: not documented.
Beginner-specific max level: not documented (game cap Lv 100).
SP gained as a Beginner after level 10: not documented (calculator returns 9 total).
Rule for putting AP into Max HP / Max MP: not documented.
Starting clothes / starting inventory: not documented.
Death EXP penalty exceptions in town or for Beginners: none documented.

Animation time of Recovery and Nimble Feet casts: "Timing unavailable".
How Recovery distributes its HP total over 30 s (tick interval): not documented.

values.text: Every character starts with 4 in each stat. You place 9 more AP at character creation, then get 5 AP per level for STR, DEX, INT, and LUK.
Total AP = 25 + 5 × (Level - 1); Free AP = Total AP - 16 (STR/DEX/INT/LUK only; the HP/MP formulas have no AP term).
AP: Earned at every level up. You get 5 per level. Used to raise STR / DEX / INT / LUK / HP / MP.

discrepancies.reason: The Beginner's guide (updated 2026-10-02) and the leveling formulas agree on the four stats, and the HP/MP guide has no AP term ("HP washing is dead in MSCW"); the glossary is a one-line definition. Whether AP can be put into Max HP / Max MP remains a documented gap (hp_mp_gain.json ap_into_hp_mp = null).
